description:
**Repro (.pi/tmp/queue-test/run_faux_tui.sh + tracing)**
1. Start TUI against FakeTransport with a held gate. Script 4 turns
   each emitting a distinct text response (response-1..response-4).
2. Type "first prompt" + Enter (run starts, gates).
3. Type "queued one" + Enter, "queued two" + Enter,
   "queued three" + Enter (each routes to Coder.steer per opi-tze.2).
4. Release the gate.
5. Telemetry trace shows 4 turns ran cleanly:
   ```
   [octo_pi_agent.turn.start] turn=1   → turn.stop reason=:stop
   [octo_pi_agent.turn.start] turn=2   → turn.stop reason=:stop
   [octo_pi_agent.turn.start] turn=3   → turn.stop reason=:stop
   [octo_pi_agent.turn.start] turn=4   → turn.stop reason=:stop
   [octo_pi_agent.loop.stop] message_count=8
   ```
6. But the TUI transcript shows ONLY response-4. Responses 1–3 are
   silently overwritten in the visible transcript even though they
   exist in the agent's message log.

**Root cause (apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex)**
finalize_assistant/3 (~L1610) and apply_partial/3 (~L1596) call
find_last_assistant/1 (L1634). That helper checks whether any
UserMessage / `{:user, _}` / ToolExecution appears **after** the last
AssistantMessage; if so, it returns `nil` and the new assistant is
appended. Otherwise it returns the index of the last assistant and
the caller **replaces** that entry in place.

For multi-turn drainage of the steering / follow-up queue:
- Turn 1's MessageEnd appends asst-1 ✓ (user msgs precede it)
- The TUI also appended {:user, "queued one"}, {:user, "queued two"},
  {:user, "queued three"} locally on each Enter — so when turn 2's
  MessageEnd lands, find_last_assistant sees those user msgs after
  asst-1 → returns nil → asst-2 appended ✓
- Turn 3's MessageEnd: the most recent boundary-bearing item is
  asst-2 (no user/tool after it in the local transcript) →
  find_last_assistant returns (idx, asst-2) → asst-2 is **REPLACED**
  with the response-3 content. asst-3 appears in place of asst-2.
- Turn 4 same: asst-3 replaced by asst-4.

End result: only the LAST assistant of a multi-turn drain is visible.

**Why it didn't show up before this work**
Previously, multi-turn drains required a tool-use turn (the only path
that drained the steering queue, see opi-tze.1). Tool turns produce
ToolExecution entries in the transcript between assistant messages,
which acts as a boundary for find_last_assistant. With opi-tze.1 fixed
and opi-tze.2's submit-routing in place, multi-turn drains via plain
text replies are now common.

**Upstream behavior (tmp/pi-mono/packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts)**
For each pending steering message, upstream emits both message_start
AND message_end events (L171-176):
\`\`\`ts
for (const message of pendingMessages) {
  await emit({ type: "message_start", message });
  await emit({ type: "message_end", message });
  ...
}
\`\`\`
The TUI receives those events and renders the user message into the
transcript at the moment the agent actually injects it. That naturally
provides the boundary find_last_assistant looks for.

Octo_pi's drain_steering_into_messages/1 in agent/loop.ex prepends to
`messages` but does NOT emit MessageStart / MessageEnd events for the
injected user messages. So the TUI never gets a chance to render an
agent-side boundary between the prior assistant and the next.

**Fix sketch**
Two complementary changes:
A. Octo_pi_agent: in drain_steering_into_messages/1 (and the
   corresponding follow_up drain), emit MessageStart and MessageEnd
   events for each injected user message, mirroring upstream
   agent-loop.ts L171-176. This restores parity for any subscriber
   that relies on the event stream as the source of truth.
B. (Optional follow-on) Octo_pi_tui: stop appending user messages to
   the local transcript inside the streaming-submit branch
   (do_handle_submit/3 with %{loader: %Components.Loader{}}); rely on
   the agent's MessageEnd event for the user message instead. That
   removes the duplicate-render risk and mirrors how the non-streaming
   submit path effectively works (the run starts immediately so the
   user msg is part of the first turn's message_end stream).

Either A alone fixes the visible symptom; B aligns octo_pi closer to
upstream's "events are the source of truth" model.

**Acceptance**
- Telemetry trace continues to show all turns running.
- TUI transcript shows ALL responses (response-1..response-N) for a
  multi-turn drain, in order.
- Existing single-turn tests still pass.
title: [BUG] Consecutive assistant turns overwrite each other in TUI transcript
